subject: Argentum pilot: tokens/sec estimate, SLO fit, and safety buffer
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@argentum.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@argentum.ai>
Date: 2025-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up after demo — expected TPS and SLOs for pilot

Hey Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency profile looked promising. Our engineering lead asked for concrete numbers so we can size the infra on our side and align procurement. A few asks:

- For the pilot (50k monthly active users, expected burst patterns attached) what tokens/sec should we budget per node for recommended model mix (base generative + retrieval enrichments)?
- We need to hit an application SLO of p95 generation latency <= 250ms for the core prompt path. Can you translate that into recommended GPU slab counts and a safety buffer (headroom %) for the pilot?
- Any constraints on payload sizes or prefix caching we should communicate to our infra team?

We want a short, executable recommendation (numbers + one-line rationale) to include in the brief to procurement.

Attaching the sample traffic profile.

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Product
Argentum Labs

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — expected TPS and SLOs for pilot

Elena — thanks for the profile, useful level of detail. Quick summary up front:

- Ballpark tokens/sec per GPU (mixed load): 8k–12k tokens/sec (A100 80GB equiv) for your prompt mix with retrieval enrichment enabled.
- To meet p95 <= 250ms at expected burst (peak concurrent 120 requests) we recommend starting with 6 GPUs (1 slab = 3 GPUs in our Dedicated offering, so 2 slabs), with a 30% safety buffer for headroom.
- If you want a conservative play (min impact to p95 under tail bursts), +1 slab (3 GPUs) for an effective 45% buffer.

Rationale and assumptions:
- Assumes average prompt + retrieved context ~900 tokens, response 220 tokens; batching kept tight for low latency (dynamic batching enabled, max batch delay 10ms).
- Measurement basis: internal microbenchmarks for the verified model combo (openLlama-2-medium-ish variant) + model quantization path.
- Caching: prefix KV caching reduces cold-start cost for repeat flows; recommend enabling prefix cache for retrieval hits (we estimate ~18% token reduction on average after warm-up).

I attached a quick token profile CSV and an XLSX with the slab math (high level). Ben and Marissa flagged a couple of model variant trade-offs — Ben, can you add the GPU mapping and canary ramp suggestion?

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@argentum.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-15T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — expected TPS and SLOs for pilot

Adding detail on GPU mapping and canary plan. TL;DR: recommended committed footprint = 2 slabs (6 x A100-equivalent GPUs); canary/warmup ramp over 72 hours; dedicated autoscale triggers for sustained 85% slab utilization.

Model mapping and numbers (concise):
- Generation model: open-llama-2-medium quantized path — ~10k tokens/sec per GPU under our latency-optimized kernel.
- Retrieval enrichment adds ~18% additional token work on average; plan for 12k effective tokens/sec per GPU when counting both inference and retrieval transforms.
- With peak concurrent 120 requests and average end-to-end tokens-per-request 1120 (900 in, 220 out), peak token demand = 120 * 1120 = 134,400 tokens in-flight/sec.
- GPUs needed (raw) = ceil(134,400 / 12,000) = 12 GPUs -> 4 slabs.
- Apply recommended pilot headroom (30%): procurement target = ceil(12 * 1.3) = 16 GPUs -> 6 slabs.

Why earlier Hannah recommended 2 slabs: she assumed more effective batching due to traffic shaping and a lower peak-concurrency after queuing. The two approaches are both valid — we should align on whether Argentum will accept queuing (latency spike) or prefer higher slab counts.

Canary ramp proposal:
- Day 0: 25% traffic to dedicated pilot (2 slabs), monitor p95 generation latency, GPU utilization, and egress token counts.
- Day 1: 50% if p95 < 200ms and util < 70%
- Day 2: 75% if p95 < 220ms and util < 80%
- Day 3: 100% if p95 < 240ms and util < 85%

Attachments: distilled XLSX with the math and a word doc for procurement language.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: argentum_gpu_headroom_estimate.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)]

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — expected TPS and SLOs for pilot

Team — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple quick decisions from our side:

- We prefer to avoid queuing-induced latency spikes for the pilot (product team asked). Please propose a procurement target. Based on Ben's compute-first math, let's move forward with the conservative recommendation: 6 slabs (18 GPUs) as procurement ask.
- Please include the canary ramp text and the three gating metrics (p95 gen latency, GPU util, token egress) in the SOW.
- Procurement wants the one-line cost estimate and a DocuSign PO path. Can you send a short note with the cost delta between 6 slabs and 4 slabs as well as a suggested billing cadence?

Marissa — looping you on the procurement language and the SOW items we want captured.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Product | Argentum Labs
